confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter (EC-6): `case 'row':     return { label: el.row.cells[rowHeaderKey(el.table)].label, from: 'row' };` under `// DECLARED BY THIS CONTRACT. Total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined`
confirmedFindings.justification: The dereference resolves against §2.3.3, the declaring shape: `rows: Array<{ row_key: string; cells: Record<string, Cell<string> | Measure | null> }>`. `Measure extends Cell<number | string>` so the Measure arm does carry `.label`, but the `null` arm does not, and a `Record<string, …>` guarantees no entry for the row-header key at all. §2.3.3's only obligation here is on the column — `is_row_header: boolean; // exactly one column MUST be true` — which is what makes `rowHeaderKey` total, not what makes the cell exist; the only other statement about it, Annex A A-17's "row headers where a key column exists", is lower precedence and is also about the column. I checked all three errata tables (§0.16 E-1…E-31, §0B.9 EB-1…EB-12, §0C.13 EC-1…EC-17) and §0C.12: no row touches §2.3.3, `TableSpec` or `cells`, and §0.19's deletion of bare UNKNOWN is scoped by its own enumeration ("Concretely: TIME_SLOT_SELECTOR.slots[].availability … APPROVAL.state"), which does not include `TableSpec.rows[].cells` — so the `| null` survives verbatim. The paragraph's own justification is therefore non-exhaustive over its declared type: it argues safety because the label "is a human string in every one of the five cell states — KNOWN, PARTIAL, NOT_MEASURED, UNAVAILABLE, PENDING", while null/absent is a sixth case the type admits. This is the same class as the two type defects Round 6 confirmed in this paragraph and is not repaired by them: keying the lookup on `el.table` rather than the envelope fixed ambiguity, not nullability. Consequence: a function declared total and non-throwing is partial, so A-2's mechanism `a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)` throws instead of evaluating for any {k:'row'} ref whose header cell is null or absent — exactly the refs produced by CLIENT_LIST (`table.rows[].row_key`), REPORT (`sections[].table.rows[].row_key`) and a degraded CHART (`table_equivalent.rows[].row_key`). Structural, not unproven, so the paragraph's NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-19/P-31 does not cover it; not security, since the failure is a fail-closed throw at EP-MINT/EP-BUILD conferring no authority. No repository claim is load-bearing (contract-internal type resolution), so no registry re-run applies.
confirmedFindings.repair: Insert one sentence in §0C.22-ter (higher precedence than §2.3.3, so the shape need not be re-typed), immediately after the `rowHeaderKey` declaration: "**The cell under the `is_row_header` column is present and non-null on every row of every `TableSpec`.** A header whose value is not yet known is a `Cell` in a non-`KNOWN` state, never `null` and never an absent key (§0.19: unknown is carried by `CellState`, never by a value domain). *Mechanism:* `validateEnvelope` asserts `rowHeaderKey(t) ∈ keys(row.cells) ∧ row.cells[rowHeaderKey(t)] !== null` for every row of every `TableSpec` reachable in the body. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`." This narrows the 'row' branch's static type to `Cell<string> | Measure`, both of which declare `label` as mint class M, restoring the five-state argument and the declared totality of `nameSourceOf`.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-bis (line 1852-1863): "interface A11yBlock { /* …role_hint, label, description, reading_order, live_region — unchanged… */ accessible_names: Record<InteractiveRef, string>;   // NEW. One entry per reading_order member; no other key admitted. }" … "Two validator rules make it total and closed: `keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order)` at `EP-MINT`, and an envelope whose `reading_order` names a ref with no entry is refused." Re-asserted verbatim by the §0C.13 errata row EC-6 and by §0C.29's P-31 row.
confirmedFindings.justification: The clause survives every escape hatch and the type error is real. (1) It is not void and not [NON-NORMATIVE]: the §0C.13 errata table's EC-6 row *restates* it — "`A11yBlock` gains `accessible_names: Record<InteractiveRef, string>` (mint class M, inside `body_hash`)" — and no row of §0.16, §0B.9 or §0C.13 touches it. Its `NORMATIVE-PENDING` on P-19/P-31 governs the UNPROVEN class only; Round 6 confirmed eight structural findings inside §0C.22-ter, a paragraph carrying the identical pending status, so pending status does not immunise a type defect. (2) The reader did not misread: `InteractiveRef` is declared exactly once in the whole artefact, at line 5653 of §4.8, as a closed six-member union of *objects* — "`type InteractiveRef = | { k: 'option'; id: string } | { k: 'field'; id: string } | { k: 'intent'; id: string } | { k: 'row'; id: string } | { k: 'entry'; id: string } | { k: 'section'; id: string };`" — and §0C.28-bis/EC-17 reaffirms it as "the typed authority", while §0C.22-ter consumes it as an object (`switch (ref.k)`, `el.row.cells[...]`). `Record<K,V>` is `{ [P in K]: V }` with `K extends keyof any`; an object union is a compile error, and every other one of the fourteen `Record<…>` uses in the contract (`Record<string, …>`, `Record<VerificationLevel, …>`, `Partial<Record<WidgetKind, number>>`, `Record<BridgeKey, …>`, `Record<AeCommitRow['family'], …>`) keys on a string/number type — this is the sole outlier, so the fences are read as literal TypeScript, exactly as Round 6's adjudication of `ReportBody`/`ScheduleBody` and `Phrase` vs `.rendered` in this same paragraph established. (3) No canonical key form exists: grep over the whole artefact finds no `refKey`, no `ref_key`, no serialisation rule, and `accessible_names[ref]` (lines 1840, 1917) is the only object-keyed index expression in the contract. The consequence is the "assertion set that can never pass" bucket: at runtime all six ref shapes stringify to `"[object Object]"`, so `accessible_names` holds at most one entry; `keys(accessible_names) === set(reading_order)` compares strings to objects and can never hold at `EP-MINT`; and the second rule refuses every envelope carrying two or more interactive refs — every `FORM` (§2.6.17 gives it `fields[].field_key`, `submit_intent`, `discard_intent`, `editor_handoff_intent`), every selector, every confirmation body. §0C.22-bis's own sentence lands on itself: "A CI check over an identifier no shape declares is the very defect EC-6 exists to close, reproduced in its own repair." The finding makes no repository claim, so no registry execution bears on it (the §0C.29 P-31 `[ABSENT]` status is uncontested and does not cure the defect).
confirmedFindings.repair: Minimal, three edits, no change to `InteractiveRef` and no new resolver. (a) In §0C.22-bis's fence, declare a key form and key on it: `type InteractiveRefKey = ` + backtick-template `${InteractiveRef['k']}:${string}`; `declare function refKey(ref: InteractiveRef): InteractiveRefKey;  // `${ref.k}:${ref.id}` — total over the closed six-member union, injective because `k` is one of six fixed tokens before the first ':'`; then `accessible_names: Record<InteractiveRefKey, string>;`. (b) Restate the two totality rules as `keys(accessible_names) === { refKey(r) | r ∈ reading_order }` at `EP-MINT`, and "an envelope whose `reading_order` names a ref `r` with no entry at `refKey(r)` is refused". (c) Rewrite the two index expressions to go through it: A-2's mechanism (line 1840) becomes `a11y.accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)`, and §0C.22-ter's closing line (1917) becomes `∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[refKey(ref)].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)`. Update the §0C.13 EC-6 row's restatement to `Record<InteractiveRefKey, string>` so the errata table and the ruling agree. (The positional-array alternative — `accessible_names: string[]` with `length === reading_order.length` — also closes it, but it re-encodes the pairing positionally and would silently mis-pair on any reorder, so the keyed form is preferred.)

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter, `'row'` branch of `nameSourceOf`: `case 'row':     return { label: el.row.cells[rowHeaderKey(el.table)].label, from: 'row' };` under the fence header `// DECLARED BY THIS CONTRACT. Total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined,` — against §2.3.3 `TableSpec`: `rows: Array<{ row_key: string; cells: Record<string, Cell<string> | Measure | null> }>`.
confirmedFindings.justification: The finding survives verification and is of exactly the class round 5 and round 6 confirmed (a member access whose type does not match the declaring shape), in exactly the newest text (`section0c.round6.bak:703` read `el.cells[rowHeaderKey(env)].label`; the current `el.row.cells[rowHeaderKey(el.table)].label` is the round-6 repair, which fixed the envelope-keyed lookup and carried the null dereference through unrepaired). §2.3.3 declares the cell value type as `Cell<string> | Measure | null`; `Measure extends Cell<number | string>` (§1.4, line 2723) so that alternative does carry `.label`, but `null` does not, and the branch dereferences `.label` unguarded while the fence header declares the function "Never throws, never returns undefined". `is_row_header` constrains only the column — "exactly one column MUST be true" — never the cell; a whole-file grep for `cells` returns the member exactly twice, the declaration at line 3158 and this dereference at line 1911, so no validator rule anywhere constrains a row's cell map for key-completeness against `columns[]` or for nullability (a `Record<string, …>` miss would also return `undefined`, violating the same sentence). §4.8's A-17 weakens rather than strengthens the case: "row headers *where a key column exists*". The row ref is reachable: `{ k: 'row'; id: string }` is a declared `InteractiveRef` member (line 5658) and §2.6.7 CLIENT_LIST's interactive paths are `table.rows[].row_key`, §2.6.10 REPORT's `sections[].table.rows[].row_key`. No exemption applies: §0C.13's errata table (EC-1…EC-10) contains no row touching §2.3.3, and §0C.2 states "Where this section conflicts … this section governs, and §0C.13 records exactly what it voids. Where it is silent, those documents stand unchanged" — so §0C.22-ter's justifying sentence that "`OptionItem.label`, `entries[].title` and a table row's header cell are all `Cell<T>`" is a false factual assertion about §2's types, not a ruling (it carries no *Mechanism* and no *Evaluation point*), and cannot void the `| null`. §0.19 deletes bare `UNKNOWN` enum members from named value domains and does not name `TableSpec.rows[].cells`. The paragraph's `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-19, P-31` marking does not cover it, on §0C.22's own ground that "a `NORMATIVE-PENDING` rule is expressly 'binding on the implementation', so it still names a field the implementation cannot have"; and §0C.12's three [NON-NORMATIVE] carve-outs do not include §0C.22-ter. Consequence as filed: A-2's mechanism (`a11y.accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref).label)` at `EP-BUILD`, and the mint-time composer at `EP-MINT`) throws on any REPORT or CLIENT_LIST envelope whose row-header cell is null instead of refusing — a function declared total that is partial, which the stated bar classes STRUCTURAL. It lowers no floor, admits no capability and relaxes no veto, so it is structural only, not security.
confirmedFindings.repair: Minimal and entirely inside 0-C — do not touch §2.3.3's other columns. Add one errata row to §0C.13 and one sentence to §0C.22-ter: (1) §0C.13 row — "**EC-6b** | §2.3.3 `TableSpec.rows[].cells` | the `| null` alternative, as applied to the `is_row_header` column | **Narrowed.** For the one column whose `is_row_header` is true, every row's cell MUST be non-null and of type `Cell<string> | Measure`; the `| null` alternative survives unchanged for every other column. §0C.22-ter"; (2) §0C.22-ter, appended to the totality argument — "**The row-header cell is non-null by rule.** For the one column §2.3.3 requires to carry `is_row_header: true`, `rows[].cells[rowHeaderKey(t)]` MUST be present and non-null in every row of every `TableSpec`; `null` remains admitted in every other column. *Mechanism:* `validateEnvelope` walks each `TableSpec` reachable from the body and refuses an envelope in which any row omits the row-header column's key or binds it to `null`. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`." No fallback expression is admissible in the branch itself: a null cell carries no `label`, and substituting `row_key` would bind the accessible name to an opaque id, breaching §1.3's "`label` … always a human sentence fragment" that the paragraph's own argument rests on.

There are two." (same stale split also in §0C.11(2): "The new branch gives them `SESSION_VERIFIED` (eight) and `ANONYMOUS` (one, `c9.no_action`)").
confirmedFindings.justification: The row describes an output the replacement mechanism does not produce. §0C.10's replacement `c9Floor` returns `maxLevel(row.min_verification, risk, C9_MODE_FLOOR(cap.mode), C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR(cap.resourceClass), CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR[row.consent_class])`, with `C9_MODE_FLOOR('READ') = 'ANONYMOUS'`, `C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR('SOURCE_READ') = 'ANONYMOUS'` and `'LOCAL' = 'ANONYMOUS'`, and `risk = def === undefined ? 'ANONYMOUS' : …` for any key not in the catalogue. Executed in the repository (`C9_CAPABILITIES` 56, `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG` 47, the non-catalogue set exactly 9), the nine are `b35.preview` PROPOSE_ONLY/SOURCE_HANDOFF, `b35.confirm` and `a22.configuration` OWNER_HANDOFF/SOURCE_HANDOFF, `c7.measurement.read`, `c8.result.read`, `b35.status`, `owner_report.status`, `owner_report.download` all READ/SOURCE_READ, and `c9.no_action` READ/LOCAL. Only the three `SOURCE_HANDOFF` keys receive `SESSION_VERIFIED` from a C9-native term; for the five `SOURCE_READ` keys every added term and the risk term are `ANONYMOUS`, so `c9Floor` collapses to `max(row.min_verification, CONSENT_CLASS_FLOOR[row.consent_class])` — and `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` is P-10 `[ABSENT]` (§A1: "both 0 hits"), so no clause pins those rows at `SESSION_VERIFIED`. "Eight" is a residue of the pre-correction draft in which `SOURCE_READ` returned `SESSION_VERIFIED` — the very raise the paragraph four lines below the table withdraws ("EC-2 first set `C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR['SOURCE_READ']` to `SESSION_VERIFIED` … It now returns `ANONYMOUS`"). §0C.11(5) states the corrected split in the same section: "the three `SOURCE_HANDOFF` keys … → `SESSION_VERIFIED`; and the five `SOURCE_READ` keys … take whatever their own `WIDGET_CAPABILITY_POLICY` row and consent class require, by (4)". The two cannot both be right, and the table is the wrong one. It is not void by any row of §0C.13 (EC-16 corrects only §0C.32's "fourteen"), is not `[NON-NORMATIVE]`, is not listed in §0C.12, and §0C.11's `NORMATIVE-PENDING` on P-11/P-24 covers whether the mechanism runs, not what it computes — so by §0.2's default the sentence is normative and it misstates its own mechanism on a table whose stated purpose is exhaustive enumeration of every floor reduction. Consequence: the contract's one audit surface for floor reductions understates five of the nine, hiding that those five fall to whatever an unpinned P-10 row carries rather than to `SESSION_VERIFIED`. (Adjudication scope: I re-read §0C.8–§0C.11-bis at lines 1330–1520, §0C.11–§0C.14/§0C.32 at lines 2330–2500, the §0C.13 errata table and the §0C.12 non-normative register in full, and re-ran the registries in process; I did not re-read all 6 088 lines for this single-finding adjudication.)

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.22-ter, the nameSourceOf fence: "case 'row':     return { label: el.row.cells[rowHeaderKey(el.table)].label, from: 'row' };   // Cell<string> | Measure", declared under "DECLARED BY THIS CONTRACT. Total over InteractiveRef. Never throws, never returns undefined", and defended by "The remaining three sources are Cell<T> ... OptionItem.label, entries[].title and a table row's header cell are all Cell<T>".
confirmedFindings.justification: The decisive text is the branch's own type annotation. §0C.22-ter annotates the 'row' branch "// Cell<string> | Measure" and its prose calls a table row's header cell one of three sources that "are all Cell<T>"; §2.3.3 declares "rows: Array<{ row_key: string; cells: Record<string, Cell<string> | Measure | null> }>" — a three-arm type whose null arm the annotation and the prose both drop, and whose Record is not required to carry an entry at every column key. The paragraph's defence ("a human string in every one of the five cell states — KNOWN, PARTIAL, NOT_MEASURED, UNAVAILABLE, PENDING") is about cell STATE, not cell ABSENCE, so it does not reach the case. A full-artefact sweep finds no clause closing the gap: is_row_header occurs only at §2.3.3 ("exactly one column MUST be true" — a constraint on columns, which is what makes rowHeaderKey total, and silent about rows), at §4.8.1's `table` role row, and inside §0C.22-ter itself; Annex A A-17 weakens the other way ("row headers where a key column exists"); no K-rule, CLIENT.n or REPORT rule and no validator requires cells to be total over columns or non-null at the header key; and no errata row (0.16 — E-7 voids only §2.3.1/§2.3.2 — 0B.9, or 0C.13) touches §2.3.3's TableSpec, while §0.18's leaf taxonomy retypes three bare strings without disturbing nullability, which §2 uses freely elsewhere (sublabel: Cell<string> | null; sections[].table: TableSpec | null). §0C.12 does not list §0C.22-ter, and its NORMATIVE-PENDING status on P-19/P-31 is expressly "binding on the implementation", so pendency is no exemption. Consequence: el.row.cells[rowHeaderKey(el.table)] is Cell<string> | Measure | null (and possibly absent), so .label is a null/undefined dereference — nameSourceOf is a partial, throwing function declared total and non-throwing, exactly the structural class "a function declared total that is partial"; under strictNullChecks the fence does not compile, and A-2's CI check at EP-BUILD crashes instead of asserting for any CLIENT_LIST, REPORT or degraded CHART envelope whose row-header cell is null — precisely the kinds whose interactive_paths produce row refs. No repository fact is load-bearing here (the finding is entirely contract-internal), so no registry re-execution bears on it. Lines read: §0C.6 in full (1812–1953), §0C.10-bis–§0C.13 (2172–2410), §1.3–§1.5 (2670–2760), §2.3–§2.3.5 (3100–3200), §2.6.7 (3470–3500), §0.5 (195–225) — about 740 lines read directly — plus full-file (6088-line) greps for is_row_header, rowHeaderKey, TableSpec, cells, header and non-null.
confirmedFindings.repair: Add one normative clause to §2.3.3 TableSpec and cite it in §0C.22-ter: "For every member of `rows`, `cells[k]`, where `k` is the key of the column whose `is_row_header` is `true`, MUST be present and non-null — a `Cell<string>` or `Measure` in any of the five states; absence or `null` refuses the envelope. *Mechanism:* `validateEnvelope`'s `TableSpec` check. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`." Then change §0C.22-ter's 'row' branch annotation from "// Cell<string> | Measure" to cite that rule alongside the "exactly one column MUST be true" rule, so `rowHeaderKey` (total over columns) plus the new rule (total over rows) jointly make the branch total and non-throwing. This preserves the paragraph's five-state argument verbatim, lowers no floor, admits no capability and widens no allowlist — it strictly narrows what may be emitted.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.10 (S0C.10, the EC-2 replacement `c9Floor`), artefact line 1393: `const def  = MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME[ref.key];     // pure data; never throws` and line 1394 `const risk = def === undefined ? 'ANONYMOUS' : RISK_FLOOR[def.riskTier];`
confirmedFindings.justification: The finding survives. §0C.11-bis declares the identifier with a concrete shape three paragraphs later, at artefact line 1523: "const MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME: ReadonlyMap<string, AiToolDefinition> = new Map(MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG.map((d) => [d.name, d]));" — and in that same fence its two siblings are accessed correctly, "C9_CAP_BY_KEY.get(key)" and "AE_CAP_BY_KEY.get(key)". A `ReadonlyMap` declares no index signature, so `MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG_BY_NAME[ref.key]` names a member no shape in the contract declares. Verified both ways: `npx tsc --noEmit --strict` on the reduced case gives "error TS7052: Element implicitly has an 'any' type because type 'ReadonlyMap<...>' has no index signature. Did you mean to call 'm.get'?", and the backend tsconfig sets `noImplicitAny: true`; executed in process against the repository (branch codex/maya-identity-consent-20260913), `byName[MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG[0].name]` evaluates to `undefined`, so `def` is `undefined` for all 56 C9-CAP keys and the named `risk` term is dead for every one of the 47 catalogue names. No errata row covers it: §0C.13's EC-2 row is the row that *installs* this text, §0C.12 does not list it, and it is not marked [NON-NORMATIVE]; its `NORMATIVE-PENDING` on P-11/P-24 bears on the unproven-claim class, not on a clause naming an undeclared member — the same standing under which Rounds 5 and 6 confirmed structural findings. The contract holds itself to exactly this rule and treats its violation as fatal: §0C.28 voids its own first draft because "§0C.11-bis declares it with exactly one member, `tryGet` ... A `.get` on it names nothing", under "the rule that 'a normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares'." The consequence is contained but real: §0C.11(2) certifies monotonicity on the ground that "the risk term is the same value from the same data, so c9Floor_new(key) ≥ c9Floor_0.13(key) pointwise by construction", and that ground is false as written because the term never evaluates. I re-verified the filer's containment claim by execution — C9_CAPABILITIES = 56, MAYA_AI_TOOL_CATALOG = 47, mode READ 41 / PROPOSE_ONLY 13 / OWNER_HANDOFF 2, resourceClass SOURCE_READ 40 / SOURCE_HANDOFF 15 / LOCAL 1, the nine non-catalogue keys identical to §0C.8's table, and the 47 tiers read 35 / medium_write 7 / high_write 2 / low_write 3 — and computed max(C9_MODE_FLOOR, C9_RESOURCE_FLOOR) against RISK_FLOOR[tier] for all 47: **zero** keys where the dead risk term would lower the floor (the 12 non-read tiers are exactly the 12 PROPOSE_ONLY/SOURCE_HANDOFF rows, contributing SESSION_VERIFIED ≥ BOUND_CLIENT/SESSION_VERIFIED). So no floor moves, C9_FLOOR_BASELINE is unchanged, and this is neither a security-contract violation nor a floor reduction — it is purely structural: a normative formula whose named term dereferences a member its declared shape does not have, and which cannot be compiled under the repository's own settings.

The paragraph's own safety argument is explicitly and only about cell *state* — "it is a human string in **every one** of the five cell states — `KNOWN`, `PARTIAL`, `NOT_MEASURED`, `UNAVAILABLE`, `PENDING`" — and about `rowHeaderKey`'s totality; it never reaches the `null` alternative. Consequence: a function whose own header declares "Never throws" is partial on values §2.3.3 admits, and A-2's mechanism `∀ ref ∈ reading_order : accessible_names[ref].startsWith(nameSourceOf(ref, env).label)` raises instead of refusing on exactly the two kinds whose `interactive_paths` emit row refs — REPORT (`sections[].table.rows[].row_key`, unconditional) and CLIENT_LIST (`table.rows[].row_key`), plus degraded CHART's `table_equivalent.rows[].row_key`. confirmedFindings.repair: Narrow the shape rather than the branch, and do it in §0C.22-ter so it outranks §2. confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.17 (EC-4), lines 1659 and 1670: "`function FLOOR_EXEMPT(i: MintedIntent): boolean {`" and "`function verificationFloor(i: MintedIntent, kind: WidgetKind): VerificationLevel {`" — the same identifier inherited from §0.13 line 152 and §0B.30 line 921.
confirmedFindings.justification: The filing is factually exact and no escape covers it. An exhaustive scan of all 6088 lines for the token yields exactly five `Minted*` occurrences — one is the prose word "Minted strings" (line 211) and the other four are `MintedIntent`, at §0.13 L152, §0B.30 L921, §0C.17 L1659 and §0C.17 L1670 — and `grep -nE "(type|interface|declare (type|interface|class))[[:space:]]+MintedIntent"` returns nothing: every occurrence is a use, none a declaration. §3.1 L3970 declares `interface WidgetIntent`, and §3.4 L4221 writes the same function as `function verificationFloor(i: WidgetIntent, kind: WidgetKind)`, so the four members `FLOOR_EXEMPT` dereferences (`priority`, `effect`, `capability`, `target`) all exist — on `WidgetIntent`, under a name the clause does not use. The contract itself makes this a violation rather than a stylistic slip: §0C.11-bis states the rule verbatim — "**A normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares**, so both are declared" — and applies the remedy by declaring; §0C.22-ter voided a mechanism on exactly this ground ("`intentOf` was also declared nowhere: it occurred exactly once in the contract, inside the mechanism that used it"), as did EC-6 ("**VOID.** `WidgetIntent` declares no `utterance`") and EC-15. Every candidate refutation fails: §0C.13's errata table has no row touching `MintedIntent` (EC-4's row amends §4.5.4 step 1, §0.13 `verificationFloor` and SOURCE.3, and names no type), and neither §0.16 nor §0B.9 does; the contract's two "deprecated alias" rules (§0.12 `required_verification`→`verification_floor`, §0.18 `LocaleText`→`Phrase`) are explicit "is read as" rulings and there is no such ruling here; the paragraph is not `[NON-NORMATIVE]` and is not listed in §0C.12; and §0C.17's `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-11, P-19` does not cure it — that marking is scoped to unproven *claims*, and §0C.22-ter carries the identical `NORMATIVE-PENDING on P-19, P-31` status yet is where round 6 confirmed eight structural findings, so the marking plainly does not immunise §0-C text against this class. The in-fence gloss "`priority` and `effect` are declared members of WidgetIntent (§3.1)" and the prose "keyed on members `WidgetIntent` already declares" identify the intended shape but are not a declaration of the type named in the signature; they also leave a real ambiguity the contract nowhere settles — whether `MintedIntent` is the full `WidgetIntent` (which carries `verification_floor`, the very field being derived) or a pre-mint subset. The finding makes no repository claim, so no registry execution bears on it. Consequence: FR-4's one enforcing mechanism under §0.55/§0B.28, as last amended by EC-4, together with `FLOOR_EXEMPT` — the predicate gating the only floor exemption the contract grants — is written over a type no shape declares and cannot be implemented as written. Lines read for this adjudication: targeted ranges 130–200, 900–960, 1335–1360, 1495–1560, 1600–1760, 1860–1950, 2400–2470, 3965–4032, 4218–4232 (~520 lines) plus token-exhaustive greps across all 6088 lines for `Minted`, `MintedIntent`, `WidgetIntent`, and every declaration form.

confirmedFindings.clause: §0C.28 EC-10, PR2 (a′): "> **PR2 (a′), normative.** The emission validator refuses any intent whose `subjectCapability(i)` satisfies `RUN_OPENING` on an envelope whose `origin` is `PROACTIVE`. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`."
confirmedFindings.justification: The clause survives every exemption route and fails the contract's own §0C.11-bis rule twice over. §0.3 S0.10 declares the only shape involved: `interface Origin { trigger: 'user_turn' | 'proactive' | 'system_reply'; … } // root member `origin``. Therefore (a) the backticked literal `PROACTIVE` names a value no shape in the contract declares — a whole-file grep finds exactly one occurrence of it, line 2150, and zero occurrences of the parallel upper-case forms USER_TURN, SYSTEM_REPLY, CLIENT_IDENTIFIED, BUSINESS_AGGREGATE, ORCHESTRATOR, SCHEDULER, CAPABILITY_READ, so no contract-wide upper-casing convention covers it; and (b) `origin` is declared as an `Origin` object, not a discriminant, so "whose `origin` is `PROACTIVE`" dereferences a struct where a scalar union member is required — the same type-level defect class as Round 6's confirmed "returns a Phrase object where §0.18 requires `.rendered`". Exemptions checked and absent: the clause is self-labelled "**normative**", carries no `NORMATIVE-PENDING` status line and no `[NON-NORMATIVE]` prefix; §0C.12 (line 2381ff) does not list it; and no row of §0.16 or §0C.13 voids or amends it — EC-10's own row (line 2414) voids the *old* §4.9.2 PR2 mechanism (a) and points at §0C.28 as its replacement, so PR2 (a′) is the live text, not the voided one. Every other statement of the identical predicate writes it correctly and case-sensitively — §3.2.5 R3.2.5 and §4.9.1 PR1 both read "`origin.trigger === 'proactive'`", §4.9.2 PR2 (b) reads "`trigger: 'proactive'`" — confirming the declared spelling and refuting any reading that the upper case is a declared alias. The contract itself makes case load-bearing (§0C.13-bis, "why the identity differs by case") and calls member-category confusion "a category error" (§0B.9). Decisively, the very next paragraph of §0C.28 corrects `c9Registry.get` to `tryGet` expressly because "a normative clause must not name an identifier no shape declares" (§0C.11-bis); that standard, applied inside this same paragraph, admits no exception for a literal that is merely obvious. The consequence is that the sole surviving normative statement of EC-10's repaired mechanism (a) cannot be transcribed into the emission validator without a reader silently substituting a member and a casing the clause does not state.
confirmedFindings.repair: In §0C.28, replace "on an envelope whose `origin` is `PROACTIVE`" with "on an envelope whose `origin.trigger` is `'proactive'`", so PR2 (a′) reads: "The emission validator refuses any intent whose `subjectCapability(i)` satisfies `RUN_OPENING` on an envelope whose `origin.trigger` is `'proactive'`. *Evaluation point:* `EP-MINT`." This matches §4.9.1 PR1, §3.2.5 R3.2.5 and §4.9.2 PR2 (b) verbatim and changes no mechanism, no membership and no floor.
